Meeting No. 37
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 1:23 PM under the chairmanship of the Honorable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, and
(1:23 PM)
The meeting of the National Assembly begins. Honorable members, names have been received to speak during Zero Hour. A time limit of one minute each has been set for speaking during Zero Hour. First, Honorable Member Kamala Pant.
Honorable Mr. Kamala Pant (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(1:23 PM)
There has been a shortage of cooking gas for many days now. In our country, which is a traditional country where we go to the roof of the house to see if the people's hearth is burning, and then go inside the house. The current government has been saying that the gas has been out for many days, and public complaints have started coming in. Today, even Honorable members discussed among themselves for a while, wondering what would happen if the gas ran out while cooking. Therefore, the government claims there is no problem with LPG gas, that there is plenty of cooking gas, but the public does not have gas at home, and it is not available when they go to buy it. What kind of problem is this? This parliament seeks an answer from the government, Honorable Chairperson. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
(1:24 PM)
Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rashtriya Janamorcha): Honorable
(1:24 PM)
Chairperson, today the public is suffering greatly from the shortage of LPG gas. The entire country's population is in a major problem due to the lack of cooking gas. Today, when they go to search for gas, it is not available at any depot, and the government is not paying attention to it. I want to draw the government's attention immediately, and I want to draw the government's attention to solve the public's problems and daily issues as soon as possible. Along with this, Deepa Nepali has been protesting for 116 days saying "Is the government's room vacant?" The government has not paid attention to that either. I urge the government to pay attention to Deepa Nepali's protest and to the related matter... (Time expired).
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Nar Bahadur Bisht.
(1:25 PM)
Honorable Mr. Nar Bahadur Bisht (Nepal Communist Party):
(1:24 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, it has been 116 days since the question "Is the government's room vacant?" was raised. It seems this government has not found a room yet. The chairman of this government's party apologized in the house. Is apologizing the job of not finding a room? And on the other hand, the government's kitchen is out of gas, people's stomachs are empty with hunger. Until when will this government, citing old laws and regulations, continue to operate? Seeing the statements of the ministers and members of parliament, one gets disgusted. Therefore, until when will this government ensure that people's kitchens have fire from gas? Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Narayan Datta Mishra.
(1:26 PM)
2
Honorable Mr. Narayan Datta Mishra (Nepali Congress): Honorable
(1:26 PM)
Chairperson, the violent incident in Devanaganj, Sunsari, is extremely serious. This should not be considered just an incident in Sunsari. It is a question of the state's security capacity and social harmony. When tension escalates between two communities, why was the security mechanism not mobilized in time? Did the government wake up like Kumbhakarna only after innocent citizens lost their lives? This is the question. My strong demand from the government is that the incident be investigated by an impartial judicial committee, and those responsible, both inside and outside, be identified and punished. Anyone spreading violence, hatred, and rumors in society in the name of caste, religion, and community should be severely punished. Saving citizens' lives is the government's primary duty, and those who boast of good governance without being able to provide security should continue to boast on social media. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson:
(1:27 PM)
Honorable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.
Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party):
(1:27 PM)
Chairperson, the government's hundred-point agenda. First, the bulldozer attack on the slum settlement under the protection of the police and army, the ordinance attack, the persecution of the judiciary. Ministers and employees are in a moral crisis. The Finance Minister's budget was overturned. The Prime Minister's anti-national statement. The moral crisis is in the public's court. Now, the appointment of political advisors in ministries and the rhetoric of good governance. Farmers are lining up in their fields due to the shortage of chemical fertilizers. Market prices have skyrocketed. The government has failed to control them. Extreme shortage of cooking gas, hearths have stopped burning. Is it better for the government to disappear than to supply? Health and education are in disarray... (Time expired).
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima".
(1:28 PM)
Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party):
(1:28 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, the hearths in many homes have stopped burning due to the shortage of LPG gas. Consumers are wandering around for gas, forced to wait in line for hours, yet they are not getting gas. During the elections, we heard that the old ones couldn't deliver. And after winning the election, we heard that now we will deliver, and we still hear that slogan of delivery. Is this delivery also just waiting in line? We don't know the literal meaning of this. Therefore, through you, Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's serious attention to fulfilling the promises made to the public during the election and until now, to provide facilities and services, and in their own words, to deliver and supply gas on time. I want to draw attention and request. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mohammad Khalid.
(1:29 PM)
Honorable Mr. Mohammad Khalid
(Janasamajwadi Party, Nepal):
(1:29 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, Siraha's Golbazar was identified as a developing commercial destination, but the recent unfortunate incidents and arson in major commercial centers have created an atmosphere of despair among the traders and investors there. The hope for the resumption of commercial activities has emerged due to the initiative of Golbazar traders, journalists, political leaders, civil society, and local administration. Many thanks to all. I want to demand from the government compensation for the damage to the commercial centers and citizens' homes burned in this unfortunate incident, and for initiatives to prevent attacks on places of faith from recurring. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(1:30 PM)
Honorable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(1:31 PM)
Millions worth of health equipment at the National Trauma Center are out of order due to neglect, so it is natural for the public to be disappointed. Whether it is the artificial shortage of LP gas, the VAT imposed on electricity, or the shortage of fertilizer for farmers, the situation does not look good. Similarly, inflation, which is becoming dire, is causing more despair than anger among the public. Honorable Chairperson, how can the public vent their anger on the government they elected by standing in line for hours and casting their precious votes? Therefore, while waiting in line for two to four hours to get LP gas might be remembered, despair is greater than anger, because anger has already been vented on the old parties. Therefore, it will take time for the sovereign Nepali people to accumulate anger. The concern is growing about how to hold the outgoing government accountable. How far is it acceptable to tamper with the law to grant immunity to one's leader? It is incomprehensible. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(1:32 PM)
Honorable Mr. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party):
(1:32 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, the hopes of the Nepali people are dashed. We heard about the tragic incident where Kedar Nath Parajuli, carrying his cancer-stricken wife Tilkumari on his back, jumped into the Sun Koshi River and her body was found. We have never heard such a thing in our lives. What has happened? Secondly, the government was running with a single majority in the House of Representatives, but we heard that the meeting was adjourned due to a lack of quorum, even though there was a majority. Hearing the news of the meeting being adjourned, the Honorable members are immature in their responsibilities... (Time expired).
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
(1:33 PM)
And (Nepal Communist Party):
Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar
(1:33 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, it is currently the monsoon season in the months of Ashar and Shrawan. Natural disasters are ongoing, but three to four months ago, a man-made disaster struck the squatters in a terrible explosive and guerrilla style, and the suffering of the squatters affected by this man-made disaster continues. They were driven away from there and kept in a holding center, and from the holding center, they were taken elsewhere, and we don't know where. The squatters have suffered from these incidents, they have suffered from this man-made disaster, but they are the real squatters. Therefore, I want to draw the serious attention of the government, through you, Honorable Chairperson, to solve their problems, and I express solidarity with Deepa Nepali, who has been sitting on a hunger strike for months saying "The government's room is vacant." Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the order of speaking during Zero Hour
(1:34 PM)
concludes here. Honorable members, names have been received on a party basis to speak during Special Time, and now I will provide time for Honorable members to speak. First, Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar. Time: 14 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honorable
(1:34 PM)
Chairperson, a few days ago, Nepali society, we Nepalis, reached a state of extremely unexpected communal clashes. The Nepali society, which has lived together for centuries without regard for religion, caste, or community, has suddenly erupted into communal clashes due to minor weaknesses. We all had to go through a great period of suspicion, and specifically, the Government of Nepal, I want to give some input to the Government of Nepal in this regard, because the Government of Nepal, although late, was able to find a way out of this incident. It was also seen that many ministers of the Government of Nepal went to the field and worked to solve the problem. Even more so, the coordination role played by the top leaders of Nepal sitting in Kathmandu is commendable. Specifically, the Government of Nepal, in the context of resolving this communal clash, Honorable Chairperson, has shown weaknesses in two or three areas. Firstly, the Government of Nepal today still thinks that the government of this country is only the federal government. The powerful politicians in this country are seen here, and the political parties of the Terai region living in the Terai, from the local heads and deputy heads to the local leaders there, and the provincial governments there, the government, without coordinating with them, sent its own personal staff to gather information and solve the problem through that, with such a raw and crude attitude adopted by the government, I personally feared greatly that this incident would escalate further, and the government's...

We were all Nepali people afraid that such immature ways of working would escalate this incident further, but with the efforts of all of us political parties, the government, religious leaders, and social leaders, this incident was resolved. However, if we look at this incident as a message, we need to analyze its two or three aspects properly.

There have been news reports that the government has reached agreements with various communities and groups related to that incident. What agreements has the government made? With whom has it made agreements? What has been agreed to be done? Nepali citizens are unaware of this, and this august Parliament, this respected Parliament, has no information about it. Therefore, through you, honorable Chairperson, I would like to strongly demand that the honorable Home Minister come to the House and inform the House about what agreements have been made with those various groups, what has been said to be done, and how much it was in the nation's interest.

Similarly, honorable Chairperson, the Government of Nepal has reached agreements with various professional communities at different times, such as with medical practitioners, nurses and health workers, civil servants, relief teachers, transport entrepreneurs, milk and sugarcane farmers, and victims of usury. However, the government appears extremely reluctant to implement those agreements, and we are afraid that Nepali society is already in such a fragile condition that a small incident can lead to major riots and communal clashes. In such a situation, if the government cannot address these issues sensitively and in a timely manner, new kinds of protests, new kinds of riots, and new kinds of movements may start again. Therefore, through you, honorable Chairperson, I would like to draw the serious attention of the Government of Nepal to this matter.

I also request that the Government of Nepal be sensitive to the implementation of the agreements made by the government and that the Government of Nepal move forward with their implementation.

Honorable Chairperson, specifically, there has been much talk about the Government of Nepal moving forward like a train on an expressway. However, regarding the daily problems of the citizens, the government seems to be working like a vehicle that doesn't even move at 10 km/h, let alone an express train or an expressway.

Regarding the supply of LPG gas, it was discussed in the assembly in various ways before. Today, friends from the districts are calling us MPs, asking us to arrange one or two cylinders of gas, saying that perhaps they will listen to you. Citizens have started requesting us. The government claims there is no problem and that the supply is smooth. How long will this government continue to deceive citizens? I would like to request the government to be more sensitive in this regard.

Similarly, regarding energy policy and tax structure, the Government of Nepal, especially concerning induction stoves, had provided many facilities to Nepali citizens through previous governments. However, this government, soon after coming into power, has broken the backs of citizens by increasing electricity taxes. I would like to request the government to be mindful of such matters. Specifically, regarding agricultural fertilizer, the crops have already been planted and paddy has been sown, yet farmers are still unable to get agricultural fertilizer. Similarly, inflation is rising, misgovernance is increasing, and farmers in the border areas are still facing various problems. However, the government is engaged in a style of excessive publicity, saying "What did you do for 35 years? We have just arrived." The government is defending itself in a style of publicity. With this kind of work, this pace, and this mentality, the Nepali people cannot be satisfied. I request the government to be vigilant in a timely manner.

Honorable Chairperson, I would also like to request another second matter. That is, Article 40 of the Constitution of Nepal clearly explains the rights of Dalits. Not only that, Article 47 clearly states in the constitution itself that these fundamental rights should be implemented by making laws within three years of the promulgation of the constitution. However, the very difficult situation is, honorable Chairperson, that the Government of Nepal has enacted some laws, such as about 16 fundamental laws, but even after 11-12 years since the constitution was promulgated, the law concerning the rights of the Dalit community has not been made by previous governments, nor has the current government prioritized making it. The biggest irony is that when the Government of Nepal was formed, we all praised that Dalits were given good space and that Dalits were made ministers, and a person from the Vadi community was brought into the government. However, even though a minister from the Dalit community is a member of the Council of Ministers, the government has presented the bill concerning the rights of the Dalit community as the lowest priority. Among the seven ministries, the Ministry of Women, Law and Justice, Children and Senior Citizens proposed the bill concerning the rights of the Dalit community as the seventh priority. If the government continues to advance the law concerning the rights of the Dalit community in this manner, there is no possibility of this law being passed for another two years. In the last election held on February 21, Dalits across the country voted for these parties based on their apologies, emotional blackmail. However, the party that promised to apologize has neither apologized in Parliament, nor brought reform programs, nor expedited the bill concerning the rights of the Dalit community, nor brought special budgets in the annual programs. Therefore, I want to clearly tell the Nepali people from here, from this house, that this government is preparing to deceive, mislead, and emotionally blackmail more than 6 million Dalits of Nepal. It is necessary for the entire Dalit community and all oppressed communities to regularly monitor this government. If that monitoring is not done, this government will also not be any new kind of government. It seems to me that this government will also delay in making laws. Therefore, I strongly demand that the Government of Nepal, as much as possible, bring the law that we ourselves passed as a proposal from the assembly and sent to the Development, Economic Affairs and Public Administration Committee, along with its report and legal framework, to the House and register it.

My final matter, honorable Chairperson, is that Nepal has been participating in various Olympic sports for more than six decades. Sports are also a major basis for empowering persons with disabilities, increasing social participation in the community, and showcasing their potential. However, at the Paris Paralympics held in Paris, France in 2024, Nepal's athlete Palisha Goverdhan won a historic bronze medal in the under 57 kg weight category, bringing honor to Nepal. Similarly, the visually impaired cricket team has also won various international games. Similarly, in other sports, including Taekwondo, Nepal's para-athletes have been participating. However, due to the failure of the Government of Nepal's Sports Act to make provisions for the rights of para-athletes and the inability to work by combining the two committees of the Paralympics, and the failure of the Government of Nepal to announce special sports-related programs, para-athletes and para-sportsmen are suffering greatly. Honorable Chairperson, I would like to draw the special attention of the Ministry of Youth and Sports of the Government of Nepal. If the government provides budget allocation in a timely manner, organizes programs, and gives them opportunities to participate in various national and international sports, they can also contribute to bringing honor to the nation and enhancing the nation's prestige. I humbly request the government for this. I end my statement here. Thank you, Namaste.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. Time: 9 minutes (13:49). After this, Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota.

Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party):- (13:49)

Honorable Chairperson, today, during this special time, I am going to raise some issues. One of these issues is a matter that has been presented as a bill, is under consideration in the House of Representatives, and will also come here. However, I am going to present it here as a precautionary step, believing that we must all be aware of the gravity of that bill, its sensitivity, and its potential far-reaching effects. This concerns the bill to amend and consolidate the laws relating to mining and minerals.

Honorable Chairperson, our country has adopted a federal system. Therefore, in terms of the distribution of various resources, gravel, sand, soil, and slate, these construction materials, these items, are kept under the local level. According to the Local Government Operation Act, 2074, Chapter 3, Section 11, Sub-section 2, (p) 7, it clearly provides for the survey, registration, permission, renewal, cancellation, and management of the excavation and use of items like gravel, sand, soil, and slate. And this is correct. Because in a federal system, there is a distribution of resources and rights, and giving that to the local level is absolutely right. However, this new government, this government that claims to have come with a strong majority, is moving forward with this bill in a way that curtails the rights of the local level.

Honorable Chairperson, if this bill is passed, it will not only reduce the jurisdiction of local levels like village and municipal governments, but it will also reduce the source of income for local levels. Similarly, it will be a fatal blow to the spirit of the federal system and will attack the federal system.

Therefore, I have raised this issue here with the intention that we, the lawmakers, and all concerned stakeholders must be aware of this bill. Although this bill may also come to our National Assembly, and we will discuss it in detail then, I felt it necessary to raise this matter at this time, so I have raised it here.

Honorable Chairperson, the federal system (Federalism) is a word derived from the Latin word 'foedus', meaning treaty, pact, covenant, alliance, etc. This federal system is definitely a distribution of rights and powers, and in a country with diversity like ours, which has various types of diversity, this is the correct system, a representative system, and an appropriate system, and a scientific system. A unitary system...

The federal system has failed here. We are adopting a federal system. Certainly, the federal system is not a panacea. It is not a magic cure, but it is a much better system than the unitary system. Therefore, we have adopted this system, and this new government is attacking this federal system. We want to alert this government.

Honorable Chairperson, I want to raise another issue, which is express vehicles. The issue of express vehicles is being discussed at this time. Perhaps express vehicles are also running at express speed. Express vehicles are definitely better than local vehicles; they reach the destination. But, while saying this, Honorable Chairperson, I remember a rule of traffic rules, a slogan that says, "Go slowly, you will surely reach; hurry, and you might not reach." If you go fast, the vehicle might hit something here and there, accidents can happen, accidents can happen, and there is no guarantee you will reach.

Therefore, if the driver of an express vehicle driving an express vehicle is good, then it is even better, it is good, they will reach the destination on time. But what if they are drunk? What if they have consumed marijuana, hemp, or datura? If the driver of such a vehicle has consumed marijuana, hemp, or datura, then I say, accidents are inevitable and damages and consequences are unpredictable. It is certain that accidents will happen with a vehicle driven by such a driver, and its consequences, its results, cannot be predicted.

Therefore, we need to understand what the differences are between express vehicles and local vehicles. And while discussing this, I feel that people have forgotten something, which is dialecticism, the class struggle. Everything is both right and wrong. I am fat, I am thin. I am fat compared to thin people, but thin compared to fatter people. I feel that this government has forgotten this dialecticism, this class struggle. Not every new thing is right, not every old thing is wrong. Among every new thing, there are both right and wrong. Among the old, there are both right and wrong. This is dialecticism, this is class struggle. We need to see what the essence of things is. In essence, while new things are indeed good, if new things again hold onto old things, then such new things cannot be accepted. Such new things cannot be right. In that case, we should say they are old. But certainly, we cannot go back now. When talking about the political system, we cannot go back.

For nearly 240 years, this country adopted a unitary system since the formation of the Nepali state, we experienced it. But as I said earlier, in a country with diversity, ethnic diversity, linguistic diversity, cultural diversity, religious diversity, and geographical and environmental diversity, a federal system is definitely appropriate. And some people, when talking about the federal system, say it will divide the country. But I want to tell those friends, if the federal system divided the country, Switzerland would have been divided first. Switzerland has not been divided. The United States of America would have been divided, but it has not been divided either. Therefore, this is nonsense, and we should not pay attention to the idea that the federal system will divide the country.

And while discussing such matters, matters of experience also come up, as do matters of knowledge. What I say is, inexperience and ignorance are not crimes. If there is no experience, it is understood. For example, I have not been a minister, I have no experience as a minister. I am not saying I want to become a minister, I am not saying this to the leader. There is no experience, that is not a crime. But in that name, under that pretext, arrogance, ego, dictatorial tendencies, the tendency to suppress everyone is not right. Yes, therefore, inexperience matters, sorry, experience matters, knowledge matters. I want to state here that one cannot act arbitrarily based on this. And as the government moves forward, did it turn back? We said that taxes on education and health are not right, but we were not heard. Did the government have to withdraw?

Education and health are things that the state should make free, as free as possible. The government, the state, must take responsibility for them. And then impose taxes on them? Such a nonsensical policy was brought by this government. But the government did withdraw it. Yes, therefore, matters of experience, matters of elders also need to be considered, need to be listened to, and I want to state that. When driving an express vehicle, it should be driven properly. If driven after consuming marijuana, hemp, or datura, or if drunk, accidents will happen. Reiterating this, I want to conclude my remarks. Thank you.

Presiding Officer: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Lila Kumari Bhandari.
(13:51 hrs)

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Samjhana Devkota, time 7 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.

Honorable Shri Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML):
(13:59 hrs)

Honorable Chairperson, today I feel that the needs and hopes of the citizens have died. I have no objection to the Honorable Ministers. I am not standing here to criticize the opposition. I am standing on this podium to present the reality of the people and to draw the government's serious attention.

Honorable Chairperson, the news of 68-year-old Kedarnath Parajuli and 67-year-old Tilkumari Parajuli of Mandandeupur Municipality-7, where the husband jumped into the Sun Kosi River with his wife, who was suffering from bone marrow cancer, has shocked us. This was not a simple suicide. I feel that the incident of Yogmaya taking Jal Samadhi in 1998 and this incident of Kedarnath Parajuli couple taking Jal Samadhi are of the same magnitude. This incident makes us question what behavior we are exhibiting towards the elderly citizens. It makes us ponder how many people are suffering from incurable diseases and whether their financial situation allows them to afford treatment. Currently, the behavior of the family, although their children might have done something for them, this is also a glimpse of the behavior of the family towards parents. Our family is moving towards nuclear families. Even though the family fulfilled its responsibilities, due to financial constraints, due to the compulsions of a poor family, he was unable to treat his wife and took the extreme step of self-immolation, Jal Samadhi, by carrying her on his back. He has left a question for the government.

How will we manage issues like free health services when education is so expensive? We are imposing taxes on health. Article 35 of our constitution states that the state must take responsibility for the health and security of citizens, but we are imposing taxes on health itself, making it impossible to get treatment. This reminds us of our responsibilities, the government's responsibilities.

I request the Honorable Ministers to be serious, to discuss this in the government, to discuss it in the cabinet, and to make it serious about how to make social security and public health services accessible and easy for everyone. The problems of the elderly are not minor problems. Our young men and women, our children are going abroad, the elderly are remaining in the villages, and they are unable to get treatment and have to give up their lives. That is why I had expressed disagreement during the budget bill and the finance bill at that time. How can I agree to this without reducing the tax on health? This was my sole stance, my party's stance. Today, this stance has become a reality. I request the government to take this seriously. When the CPN-UML brought up social security, old-age allowance, and gave assurance that the government would be a support for the elderly, today, unable to feel that, the elderly have had to take Jal Samadhi. I want to say that the government should handle this properly.

Furthermore, on Asar 24th, Ganesh Nepali of Mugu committed self-immolation, and the government's commitment and the nine-point agreement made by the government following that self-immolation have not been implemented to date. Just yesterday, the entire family of Ganesh Nepali was wandering at the Singha Durbar gate without a pass. They say, "The government has not provided us with any assistance. Our agreement with the government has not been heard." We made a nine-point agreement to form an investigation committee, then provide relief and compensation, manage travel expenses for family and relatives from Mugu to Kathmandu, provide employment to the wife, educate the children up to higher education, manage the funeral expenses by the government, even declare them a martyr, and for the family to take the body after the post-mortem. We have not received any response from the government to date. Today, his mother, father, relatives, brother, and the entire family might have come to the Singha Durbar gate. I want to ask the government what agreements were made and why they were not implemented? When will they be implemented? I want to draw the attention of the concerned ministry and the Home Minister, as the Home Minister himself made the agreement, to be serious, to come to this respected house and provide information, at what stage it is, when the agreement was made, what agreements were made, what is in the process of implementation, and when the implementation process will be completed.

Similarly, on Shrawan 10th, in Dewangunj, Sunsari, Jayaprakash Mehta and Omprakash Mehta, among others, were killed by police firing by the government. An agreement has also been made with them. What are the terms of that agreement and when will it be fulfilled? I want to draw the government's attention to provide information about that in this parliament as well. I want to draw the attention of the Home Minister and the Home Ministry. Through you, Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw attention to get this resolved as soon as possible and inform this respected house. Today, while I was cooking, my own gas ran out at home. What should I tell the traders? "Honorable Sir, if you, your government, send gas, then I will give it." Currently, despite the fault, it has been rumored that the opposition parties have created a gas shortage by hoarding it in their businesses. Is this true, Honorable Minister? If it is true, we are ready to answer. If it is not true, then Honorable Minister (..time expired.)

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini, time 10 minutes. After this, Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai.

Honorable Shri Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):
(14:06 hrs)

Honorable Chairperson, first of all, I offer my heartfelt condolences to the sons of Nepali mothers who lost their lives in the incidents that occurred in districts like Sunsari, Siraha, etc. I also wish for the speedy recovery of the injured and express my heartfelt sympathy to the bereaved families. I want to demand from the government that free health treatment for the injured and relief for the victims be arranged.

The policies, style, arrogance, and behavior of the government formed with nearly a two-thirds majority...

Because the overall situation including economic, social, religious, political, judicial, and administrative sectors has reached a disappointing state.

For ages, religious and ethnic communities have lived together in harmony. However, the government has appeared indifferent towards skillfully resolving minor disputes that arise between religious and ethnic communities in a timely manner, leading to a situation where communal harmony is being disrupted in various districts of the Terai. The government's excessive use of force has resulted in the loss of lives of promising youths. I want to draw the government's attention to investigate the truth of the incident, take action against the culprits, and strengthen communal harmony further by forming a high-level parliamentary inquiry committee. In the future, I want to draw the government's attention to refrain from any act that disrupts communal and ethnic harmony. Nepal, an agrarian country, known as the granary of the country, is facing declining food production due to the lack of timely irrigation, fertilizer, and seeds in the Terai Madhesh region. Nepal, which used to be self-sufficient in food, is now increasingly dependent on food imports. The ministers who promised to do in 100 days what couldn't be done in 35 years did not pay attention to ensuring the easy availability of fertilizer required by farmers during the paddy planting season. We are hearing reports of poor farmers who went to buy fertilizer being jailed in India and just recently released. On one hand, the farmers' production capacity is decreasing, and the problems of fertilizer, pesticides, and seeds, as well as technology, persist. On the other hand, consumers are forced to eat fruits and vegetables containing pesticides. Due to the unnatural price rise in food grains, the poor, landless, and middle-class people are unable to afford even one meal a day.

Honorable Chairperson, due to the government's flawed policy of silencing and ignoring, investors are living in fear and anxiety. Industries and factories are closing down, and the situation is becoming increasingly dire. Capital flight is increasing. The government, which claims to attract foreign investment, is instead discouraging domestic capital investment instead of stopping it. Can economic prosperity be achieved in five years in this manner? I want to ask the government a question. Although we have seen the Home Minister issue strict directives not to ask questions, questions are still being raised in the parliament. Nevertheless, I want to draw your attention to consider this seriously. In the local government, the bureaucracy, which is the permanent government, has seen an increase in irregularities in the name of reform. Their morale is being lowered. Not only the public but also government officials and employees are being presented as rulers rather than servants, and I disagree with these aspects of the bill. Therefore, I request that this bill be sent to the Law and Justice Committee for in-depth discussion. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima". (15:03 hrs) Honorable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Communist Party of Nepal): (14:04 hrs) The Bill relating to the Control of Infectious Animal Diseases, 2083 has been introduced. Honorable Speaker, I believe its intention is good. However, after the honorable minister presented it for discussion, it must be debated. But some of its theoretical aspects, its bill number is not mentioned here. To consider this document official, there is no signature of the minister, no seal of the Government of Nepal, no signature of the Chief Secretary, no signature of the ministry's secretary. Nothing at all. Such a document has been distributed to us, what is this? I would like to draw the attention of the honorable minister through the honorable speaker regarding this. The objectives of this bill are to reduce or prevent the damage incurred by farmers from diseases in domestic or wild animals, to minimize or control zoonotic diseases, to clarify the jurisdiction of the federal, provincial, and local governments in controlling animal diseases, and to promote the export of healthy animal products. This bill was necessary, and I welcome it. However, the federal government has more authority, but the bill places a heavy burden of disease control on the provincial and local levels. Animal insurance is not mentioned, and there is no clear provision on whether insurance payments will be received or not. There is ample room for suspicion that the definition of animal epidemic may make the government arbitrary. How many deaths constitute an epidemic? After what rate of transmission to humans should it be declared an epidemic? Such provisions are not present. If any official or the government feels like calling it an epidemic, they can declare it an epidemic, and farmers will suffer great losses. There are other means by which animal diseases can spread, such as milk, meat, and feed related to animal products, which are not clearly mentioned here. Therefore, I feel that transportation also needs to be discussed. Now, in the definition, wild animals are also mentioned as animals, but the responsible body for their care is only the Department of Animal Services. The role of the Department of Forests and the National Parks Department, which look after wild animals, is not mentioned, and I wonder how that will be managed. I feel that this delegated authority from the ministry to the Government of Nepal should be removed. We will discuss it. I request that it be sent to the Law Committee, and finally, I would like to suggest that instead of just "animal" in the name of the bill, it might be better to call it "livestock and poultry," thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable member Narayan Datta Mishra. (14:07 hrs) Honorable Mr. Narayan Datta Mishra (Nepali Congress): Honorable Speaker, discussing the Bill relating to the Control of Infectious Animal Diseases, the agricultural profession of Nepali farmers is a traditional and gradual profession. Livestock farming is connected to the lives of Nepalis. It would not be an exaggeration to say that millions of farmers' income, employment, and livelihoods depend on this profession. Therefore, controlling animal diseases is not only a shield to protect the lives and property of farmers and the country's economy but also a great support. Thus, the main objective of the bill should be to prevent diseases from occurring rather than controlling them after they have occurred. For this, regular vaccination programs must be made mandatory and effective. At the local level, monitoring should be done, laboratory testing should be prompt, and reporting should be accurate. Based on past experiences, the early warning system for disease control needs to be improved. The practice of creating a commotion only after the disease has spread should be discouraged. If timely attention is not given to prevent the situation of destroying animals, farmers can suffer great losses. Compensation should be provided. There is a need for legal commitment for a transparent, fast, and less cumbersome compensation process for farmers. If animal and animal product movement at the border is tightened, the possibility of diseases entering from outside will be reduced. Animal quarantine must also be strictly followed. Furthermore, the responsibility for disease control should be made more accountable to the provincial and even local levels than the federal government. Therefore, the responsibilities of the federal, provincial, and local levels need to be clarified. We pay great attention to making laws, but some laws remain in the drawers, only adorning them, rather than being implemented. If the results of the law reach the farmers' sheds, it will be a successful law. I say again, saving animals means saving farmers, saving farmers means not only saving the rural economy but also taking farmers towards prosperity and making the country self-reliant in agricultural products. Finally, while supporting the theoretical objectives of this bill, it needs to be further refined and developed by sending it to the committee for clause-by-clause discussion, making it farmer-friendly, compensation-oriented, scientific, and implementable. Thank you. Honorable Speaker: Honorable member Rukmini Koirala. (15:00 hrs) Honorable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): (14:00 hrs) Bill prepared to make provisions regarding infectious animal diseases, 2083. Honorable Speaker, this bill is important for addressing animal health, public health, food security, and international trade. I welcome it. This bill attempts to create a legal basis for the coordinated system between federal, provincial, and local levels for the prevention, control, monitoring, eradication, and emergency management of animal and animal product diseases, which is a positive aspect. Currently, farmers in our country raise cows, buffaloes, goats, sheep, yaks, mules, ducks, chickens, and fish. However, at times, bird flu, which affects poultry, has also appeared in humans, and rabies transmitted through dog bites has caused human deaths. Foot-and-mouth disease, PPR, classical swine fever, hoof-and-mouth disease, African swine fever...

FMD, Lumpy Skin, Glanders, African Horse Sickness, Fish Diseases, and 20 other diseases worldwide seem to require compensation and relief to be included in the regulations. Due to the number of such diseases, the infection of animals, and the decrease in production and productivity, farmers suffer financial losses of thousands annually. Losses from Foot and Mouth Disease alone amount to 7 billion rupees, approximately 8 billion rupees from various parasitic diseases, and rabies, tuberculosis, bird flu originating in birds, swine flu, Ebola, SARS, Corona, and COVID-19 pandemics have spread from birds to humans. This bill clearly provides for prompt disease notification, surveillance, sample collection and testing, declaration of infected areas, movement control, and emergency response. The provision for clear division of work, duties, and authority among the federal, provincial, and local levels appears consistent with the federal governance system. It seems that all matters should be clarified in the definitions themselves. Compensation Provision: It appears that the basis, procedure, valuation, and payment time and limits for compensating livestock owners if animals have to be culled for disease control should be mentioned in the bill itself. Disease Control Fund: There appears to be a need for the source, operation, transparency, auditing, and expenditure of the fund. The basis for infection (...) should be clearly mentioned. Time is up. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. (15:09) Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress):- Honorable (15:13) Approximately 62 percent of households in Nepal are engaged in agriculture. According to various government and study sources, about 50 to 66 percent of the population depends directly or indirectly on agriculture and animal husbandry. Data shows that more than 3.4 million farming families are involved in animal husbandry. Agriculture and animal husbandry are major sources of employment and livelihood. Nepal is an agricultural country. Animal husbandry in Nepal is not just a part of the agricultural sector; it is also a sector linked to the employment, income, and livelihood of millions of farmers. Infectious diseases spreading among animals can affect not only a farmer's shed but the entire animal husbandry sector and the larger economy. Therefore, preventing diseases is the need of the hour rather than controlling them after they occur. Honorable Chairperson, the coordination between the federal, provincial, and local levels is a positive aspect of this bill. The provision for declaring national-level disease control programs, disease-free zones, and compartments, and facilitating the international trade of animal products is also important. While linking animal health with public health and environmental health is even more positive, enacting laws alone is not enough. Farmers' safety and necessary financial support, resources, and materials must be ensured. Culling animals for disease control is a loss of farmers' hard work and investment. Therefore, a provision for fair, timely, and transparent compensation to farmers when animals are culled due to disease must be clear in the bill. We must prioritize biosecurity. Instead of culling after the disease occurs, we need to strengthen measures to prevent the spread of diseases through farm sanitation, quarantine, movement control, regular testing, and vaccination. The bill also needs to effectively address diseases of fish and aquatic animals. Significant investment is being made in aquaculture in Nepal; provisions for disease control, testing, and compensation in that sector must also be clear. Similarly, diseases like mastitis, which regularly cause significant financial losses to farmers, need to be given adequate priority in disease control policies. Another important issue is testing after disease identification, the decision to cull animals, its criteria, the process of informing farmers, and compensation. All these must be clear, scientific, and transparent. Farmers must also know why their animals were culled. They should not have to spend years going to offices for compensation. Animal health is linked to farmers' health, food security, public health, and the national economy. Therefore, it must be advanced according to the concept of food and health security. This program was initiated during the tenure of former ministers Ramnath Adhikari and Beduram Bhusal. The main objective of the bill is positive, but compensation for farmers and free and regular vaccination, biosecurity, fish and aquatic animals (... time is up.) Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari. (15:16) Honorable Mr. Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party):- (15:17) Honorable Chairperson, I wish to express my views on the theoretical discussion of the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, presented by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment. The livestock and poultry sector is the backbone of Nepal's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), food and nutrition security, and especially the rural economy. Due to epidemic diseases like Foot and Mouth Disease, Lumpy Skin Disease, Bird Flu, and African Swine Fever, our millions of farmers suffer billions in losses annually. At a time when zoonotic diseases are also posing serious risks to public health, this bill brought by the government to create an integrated and scientific legal framework is timely. I believe that once this act is in place, it will contribute to improving public health and promoting international trade of Nepal in line with the objective of healthy animals and meat products. The government states that this bill has been brought to make legal provisions regarding infectious animal diseases (control) under the federal government's exclusive authority listed in Schedule 4 of the Constitution concerning quarantine and communicable disease control, the shared authority of federal and provincial governments in Schedule 7 concerning veterinary services, and the shared authority of federal, provincial, and local governments in Schedule 9 concerning agriculture. When enacting federal laws, they must be made in a way that does not impede the shared and exclusive authorities of the federal, provincial, and local governments. Provisions that contradict the legislative act must be removed. The provisions for relief if infected or suspected animals/products are culled should not be complicated in the bill. It is not practical to expect rural small farmers who raise two to four cattle for their livelihood to complete 100 percent of the paperwork if they do not have an animal health certificate or if there are other technical deficiencies. If the compensation process becomes cumbersome, farmers will be tempted to hide diseases, which will further help the epidemic spread. Therefore, I request the government through the Honorable Chairperson to send this bill to the legislative committee for clause-by-clause discussion, enriched with further suggestions and consultations from experts, livestock farmers, and stakeholders, to make the relief system simple, transparent, and hassle-free, and to make it practical, people-oriented, and farmer-friendly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Basudev Ghimire. (15:21) Honorable Mr. Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, first of all, I would like to thank the Honorable Minister of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment for bringing the bill related to infectious animal diseases. In our country, more than 80 percent of the population relies on animal husbandry as a profession, a source of income, and a means of livelihood. Therefore, the bill to control it was necessary. This bill should clearly provide for the culling and testing of animals suffering from epidemic diseases. Clear provisions regarding fish farming and aquatic animal diseases should be made. Provisions for disease prevention through biosecurity should be rewarded before animals contract diseases. Although there is a provision for relief to livestock owners when animals are culled by the government after contracting infectious diseases, I see a need to make a provision for relief when animals die due to epidemics, as this provision is not in the bill. Similarly, I urge the government through the Honorable Chairperson to send this bill to the legislative committee for discussion on various points, as it appears necessary to make it a very good pillar for the country's income and source of income. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar. (15:23) Honorable Mr. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party:- (15:23) Honorable Chairperson, the motion to consider the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, presented by our Honorable Minister, is before us. Actually, I feel the name of this bill might not be appropriate. Secondly, is this a bill or a concept paper for making a bill? This also causes confusion. Because it is coming as a concept. It only mentions what topics are included, what content is included. Therefore, it seems that the conceptual framework itself is not aligned. Secondly, this bill has come, it has no stamp, nor the signature of the Honorable Minister or Secretary. Therefore, it seems like it is just a concept paper that has not yet been finalized as a bill. It should be understood in that way. Secondly, Nepal is an agricultural country; we have the tradition of traditional agriculture, animal husbandry, and poultry farming. That is not very organized, and the state's attention was not reaching there, and now gradually these industries or farms are developing. Along with this, large-scale infections like animal infections, poultry infections, and fish infections are occurring, causing farmers to incur losses, and farmers are less motivated to work. At such a time, this bill has been put forward. This is important, and we will discuss the issues within it during the clause-by-clause discussion. Looking at it now, it is indeed progressing towards the business of animal and poultry farming, but there are not enough laboratories, no quarantine facilities, and we have open borders. For this reason, farmers are not getting much enthusiasm, and farmers are also facing difficulties in receiving compensation from the state when animals and poultry are culled in the process of preventing various diseases that are emerging. (... time is up.) Honorable Chairperson:- Honorable Member Dharmendra Paswan. (15:26) Honorable Mr. Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, I am speaking during the discussion on the Infectious Animal Disease Bill, 2083. I would like to thank the Honorable Minister very much for this bill, which was prepared by former minister Ramnath Adhikari and has now reached the floor of the house through the Honorable Minister. There are five or six points in this. This seems like a very serious matter. First of all, we are in a federal system, this is against federalism, it needs to be included. Another point is the issue of farmer compensation, I will state it clearly. There is a lack of clear authority and responsibility between the federal, provincial, and local levels.

6. The problem of disease and the weakness of the early detection and information system are evident. The transportation system for emergency disease control is not in place. The compensation system for livestock owners and farmers is inadequate. The surveillance of animals and animal products at border crossings is weak, and due to open borders and uncontrolled movement of animals and animal products, there is a risk of infectious diseases entering. Quarantine and border surveillance need to be made more scientific and effective. The role and authority of veterinarians and technical manpower need to be clarified, which is not evident here. Furthermore, regarding the committee concept that has been proposed, there is no representation from the provinces. When forming this committee, it is essential to have representation from all seven provinces. Another issue is the need to strengthen the system for addressing new and emerging infectious diseases. With the increasing risk of new diseases due to climate change, international trade, and animal movement, the One Health concept, coordination of human, animal, and environmental health, and strengthening modern laboratories and risk-based disease surveillance are necessary. Also, since this bill is an incomplete document, should it be revised and resubmitted? Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I wish to share a small notice. (15:30 hrs) I wanted to inform you that the original copy of this bill that we received has the ministry's stamp and the minister's signature. However, the legislative branch printed a different copy from a digital source, and this is what was distributed. I just wanted to provide this information. I have also shortened the minister's speech for the honorable minister's convenience. Honorable members, the discussion on the motion to consider the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, will now conclude. Honorable members, I will now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forest, and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary, to respond to the issues raised in the discussion. Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forest, and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary: (15:31 hrs) Honorable members, Mr. Chairperson, all honorable members present today, the majority of the issues raised by honorable members during the theoretical discussion on the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill are positive. I would like to state that the necessary issues can be included during the clause-by-clause discussion in the committee, including the proposed amendments, to further enrich or improve this bill. Before I respond, I would like to briefly provide a little background. The livestock and poultry sector in Nepal is, as you have all stated before and as I have mentioned, the basis of livelihood for millions of households. Infectious diseases in this sector cause livestock deaths, reduce production, and negatively impact farmers' income and the overall economy. Diseases that have appeared in recent years, such as African Swine Fever, Lumpy Skin Disease, Bird Flu, as well as long-standing diseases like Foot-and-Mouth Disease, PPR, and Rabies, have had a significant impact from the local to the national level. Among such diseases, zoonotic types like Rabies, Tuberculosis, and Japanese Encephalitis affect not only animals but also human health. In the current context, where the health of animal products consumed by the public is also challenged due to such diseases, it was necessary to address these diseases not just as veterinary issues but as a shared concern of animal, human, and environmental health under the One Health concept. In this regard, the existing legal provisions are somewhat insufficient. Currently, in Nepal, infectious diseases of livestock, poultry, fish, and zoonotic diseases are managed under the Animal Health and Livestock Services Act. However, after the country adopted a federal governance system and with the recent increase in commercialization of animal husbandry and foreign trade of animal products, the existing legal provisions with limited scope are insufficient to address these issues comprehensively. Furthermore, even within the federal system, there is ambiguity about who is responsible for what, leading to delays in disease diagnosis and control, which further spreads the disease and increases the possibility of significant damage. Therefore, to clearly define the responsibilities of all three tiers of government, to identify diseases promptly, to mitigate outbreaks, and to control infectious diseases of livestock, poultry, and fish, a clear legal framework is necessary. Hence, the Government of Nepal has presented this bill in this esteemed house. Regarding the objective, we brought this bill with the primary objective of early detection and information dissemination, surveillance, prevention, control, and eradication of infectious and epidemic diseases in the livestock, poultry, and fisheries sectors in Nepal. Another objective is to create a legal basis for the effective implementation of the One Health concept by establishing clear coordination among relevant bodies at the federal, provincial, and local levels, and to control the spread of diseases by identifying infected animals and products and regulating their movement, and to provide relief and compensation to farmers who suffer losses, and to manage and dispose of infected animals and products safely. Regarding the issue raised by Honorable Member Pram Dangal about establishing a relief fund for animal epidemic control, this can be discussed. Regarding the availability, accessibility, and quality of veterinary medicines, I would like to inform you that the Animal Medicine Act, 2035, makes provisions for the regulation of veterinary medicines. Regarding the control of epidemics in wildlife, as raised by Honorable Member Garima, arrangements can be made in coordination with the relevant departments that handle wildlife. The suggestion to regulate the transportation of items other than animals that spread diseases, such as milk, meat, feed, and bedding, is positive, and I thank you for it. Regarding the suggestions made by Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra, they are very positive, and I would like to inform you that this act seeks to provide more authority to local and provincial levels. I would also like to inform you that further discussion can be held on the role of the department in the event of a declared epidemic. Similarly, regarding Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota's point about controlling the spread of disease from one animal, I would like to inform you that this has been emphasized because it affects the health of other animals and humans. Regarding Honorable Member Basudev Ghimire's point about strengthening laboratory facilities and ensuring access for farmers, it is positive, and I would like to inform you that the government provides 75% of the premium for animal insurance. Regarding Honorable Member Dharmendra Paswan's question, this act largely delegates authority to provincial and local levels. I would like to clearly inform you that the responsibilities of all three tiers are within the scope of epidemic or infectious disease situations, and there is also a provision for provinces to form committees. I would like to inform you that these matters can be further discussed and moved forward. I would like to thank you for providing valuable information and for clarifying any points that may have been missed. For now, I would like to conclude my remarks by responding to the questions raised by the honorable members. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the motion to consider the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, is now concluded. Honorable members, I will now put to vote the motion to consider the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083. Honorable members who are in favor of this motion will say "Aye". Honorable members who are against this motion will say "Nay". Honorable members who are in favor of this motion, say "Aye". "Aye" The voices of "Nay" were not heard. Therefore, I declare that the motion to consider the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, has been approved by consensus. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that those who wish to present amendment proposals on the Infectious Animal Disease (Control) Bill, 2083, can do so in accordance with Rule 106 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Honorable members, this meeting is now adjourned until Thursday, the 28th of Shrawan, 2083, at 1:15 PM.
